entry.title: Homura-Hime v0.4.3
entry.content:
Plugin release: A connection screen styled like the game, a Server window for commands, controller support for connection UI, and fixes for reconnecting, Death Link and the death menu. See README for installation instructions.
**Update the plugin and the .apworld together.** The world only changes its version number: seeds from 0.4.1 and 0.4.2 play with this plugin without generating anything new (checked against real slot data of both), and saves and server records are not touched.
### New:
**The connection screen (F10) is a full-screen menu in the game's own style:**
- It uses the look of the title screen's Continue menu - **Server window:** the right side shows what the server says (command results, chat, hints for you, the items you send and receive) and has a box to type into. Enter sends the text as your slot: `!hint`, `!collect`, `!getitem`, ordinary chat. - **Keyboard:** Up/Down move through the fields and buttons, Left/Right move between the left column and the Server window (Left returns to the item you were on), Tab goes through everything, Enter does what the selected item does, Ctrl+V pastes, F11 connects, F12 disconnects, Esc closes. - **Controller:** the D-Pad (or left stick) moves, A does what Enter does, B or Start closes. Hold **Start, Select, LB, RB, LT and RT** together to open the screen without a keyboard. - **More readable disconnected text:** the text containing the plugin version and instructing how to open the Server Connect menu has a style background and is larger and more readable now. It returns to being small and unintrusive when connected
### Fixes:
- **Reconnecting gave the same items again.** Connecting again while playing (a manual disconnect and connect, or pressing Connect twice) put the progress stored in the game's save file back over the live progress, so items received since the last save were granted a second time. The same went for unlocked chapters, progressive keys, cleared worlds and anything set aside. The stored progress now only replaces the live one when the game loads a save or you switch to another save or slot. Locations checked while offline are still sent when you connect. - **Death menu:** after a Death Link death the death menu could fail to appear when tabbed out and leave the game stuck. The game re-evaluates the menu when it is lost. - **Death Link messages** no longer name the enemy that killed you; they say that you died, like the other games do, so a message sent to other players is no longer wrong about the cause. - Connecting no longer fails because of keys the game did not receive: F11, F12 and Esc are read from the game's update, so they work with an input method or a keyboard tool running. - Connecting twice from one key press no longer connects twice; the log says what is going on ("Connecting to ... as ...", "Connect ignored: ...", "Disconnected from Archipelago").
### Changes:
- The setup guide and READMEs describe the new connection screen and the controller combination. - Tests for the new screen's logic (focus, controller edge detection, the console log, the death menu, the death cause) and for reading the slot data of real 0.4.1 and 0.4.2 seeds.

entry.content:
# Spyro: A Hero's Tail v2.3.0: The "I Could Barely Fit the Full Changelog" Update As is becoming tradition, v2.3.0 has *way* more than was originally planned. My to-do list is almost completely empty now, but there is just barely enough to justify a v2.4 probably not super long into the future, depending on irl factors.
[Setup Guide](<https://github.com/PhoenixAki/PhoenixAP/wiki/Spyro:-AHT-1-%E2%80%90-Setup-Guide-&-FAQ>) ## Hotfix 1 (11/12/26 at approximately 7:15PM EST) - Fixed an issue that led to Universal Tracker occasionally reporting incorrect info when evaluating glitched logic. - Added convenience client command `/enabled_tricks` that outputs all tricks enabled for this seed. - Fixed an issue with & re-wrote the code that ensures `dragon_eggs_goal` and `light_gems_goal` aren't set too high as a result of `exclude_chest_items` and/or `minigame_checks`. - Fixed Global Lockpicks not increasing in-game when received due to an item name client typo. - Fixed Red's Laboratory Lockpicks generating a client error due to an off-by-1 client typo. - Updated game mod files to v22.1, which is a non-critical update that fixes 2 things: - When cannons are locked, the Icy Camp cannon no longer shows the :b: symbol above it still. - When using level lockpicks, the pause menu lockpick counts now turn green to make it easier to tell when all are collected.
# Changelog (compared to v2.2.2) ## Most Notable - AHT AP now supports 31 different tricks via `enabled_tricks`. Each one is an alternative logical path to different regions or locations in the game. - This comes with glitched logic on the tracker page. Things that are possible to do, but only through a trick that you don't have enabled, will display as "glitched". - This also comes with, unsurprisingly, a large number of logic adjustments. Most changes were small in scope to support tricks, but some areas got their logic completely rewritten (Red's Lab being the most impacted). - New option `item_bundles` lets you bundle Dark Gems, Global Lockpicks, or Light Gems together so you receive multiple at a time. - New option `cannon_lock` lets you lock the ability to use cannons behind a "Cannon Unlock" item. Minigame cannons are not affected. - On a related note, "Turret" minigames have been renamed to "Cannon" now, to be more consistently named. - New option `minigame_checks` replaces `vanilla_minigame_rewards`. It allows you to partially or fully disable each type of minigame. - New option `chest_keys` replaces and is an expansion of `key_rings`. It allows you to choose from now 4 different ways to unlock chests. - Pay careful attention to your YAML. Many options have had their settings altered for various reasons. - More code refactoring than I could ever hope to list here. The most heavily rewritten areas include the generator's code for creating items, the client's code for processing received items, and the generator's code for handling edge cases (`auto_corrections` stuff), but almost everything was touched at least a little bit. ## Less Notable - New option `disguise_shop_items` replaces `hide_shop_item_names`. It allows for further hiding of shop item information. - `trap_length` has been expanded slightly to allow for individual customization of each type of trap's length. - Added 11 YAML presets, mostly intended to show off notable features or to minimize/maximize certain types of items. - Condensed the 6 min/max range options for randomized costs into a single option called `random_costs`. - Expanded the "Breath Bombs" filler category so that each type of bomb is individually choosable. They also now use their vanilla game models instead of lockpicks. - DeathLink can now temporarily be disabled in the client using `/toggle_deathlink`. - A number of options that were previously unable to be randomized now can be. - Options Creator is supported again. Previous update(s) introduced some option types that weren't compatible, but I have fixed that now. - In the event a new save file is needed, map icons will now correctly reflect current logic. Similarly, the shop is synced so that already-bought items will appear as bought. - Shop items now properly list in ascending order on the tracker page. ## Fixes - Fixed a client bug where if a host sent multiple copies of an item via `/send` or similar, only the first one would get processed. - Fixed a client memory error that would occur if connecting to an AP room that is password protected. - Fixed a niche issue impacting seeds that have no goal and are fixed by `auto_corrections`, in which the client wouldn't get the memo about the fix. - Strengthened the client's logic so the game is not patched if there is a mismatch between versions, and the Dolphin process is properly unhooked when disconnecting. - Fixed the client not properly logging to a .txt file.

entry.title: FTL: Faster Than Light v0.6.0
entry.content:
Every seed gets its own save, fights and events send checks, four new traps, two new events, new options to change how a run feels, and a dashboard that knows the logic. Plus a lot of fixes from your reports during the betas.
## Updating from 0.5
1. In ftlman, replace `ArchipelagoFTL.ftl` with the one from this page and click Apply. 2. **Copy the Hyperspace library from this page into the FTL folder again**, after Apply: `Hyperspace.dll` (Windows), `Hyperspace.1.6.13.amd64.so` (Linux, Steam) or `Hyperspace.1.6.12.amd64.so` (Linux, GOG/Humble). 0.6 needs this new one. 3. Replace `ftl.apworld` too, and make a new seed: the new options only exist in a seed made with 0.6. Archipelago 0.6.7 is needed.
On Epic, FTL has to be downgraded to 1.6.9 by hand first, see the setup page.
## Saves
- **Every seed has its own FTL save**, one per slot. When you join a new seed the mod asks first, and the old save stays exactly as it was. Your normal FTL save is never touched. - A **Saves** button on the main menu lists them all, with their checks and when you last played. Load one, run in progress included, or archive it.
## New checks
- **Fights per sector** (`combat_checks_mode: per_sector`): the first fights you win in each sector send their own checks, 1 to 5 per sector. - **Archipelago Event checks** (`event_checks`, 5 by default): the relay and pirate events hand out their own checks. Every sector gets one of them for sure. - **Reactor checks** (`reactor_checks`): reactor power 10, 15, 20 and 25. - Accepting a surrender counts as a fight won, an enemy that jumps away does not.
## New options
- **Sector Skip**: a layout that already reached the next sector can skip sectors 1 to 4. Their first beacon is an exit, and jumping right away gives 60 scrap and one more pick in the start-of-run menu. - **Sector Locks**: each layout needs two Sector Passes, to leave sector 4 and sector 7. - **Flagship Sabotage** (0 to 5): each Flagship phase arrives weakened, less hull, shields or weapons. - **Archipelago Shop Deal Scrap** (0 to 200%): what the deals pay, 0 turns them off. - **Kestrel Needs Its Key**: when you don't start with the Kestrel, it needs its key like any other ship. Until it comes, the hangar marks it NO KEY and START refuses it. - **Progressive Unlocks the System**: the first upgrade of a system also unlocks it, so systems come sooner. - **Layout Unlocks**: `independent` (a Type B or C can come without the A) and `progressive` (one key per layout, A then B then C). - **Early Ship Keys** (1 by default): a second ship comes early, in your own first checks. - **Event Beacons**: which beacons say ARCHIPELAGO on the map. - **Crew Names**: crew who join take the other players' names, or the team's, or FTL's. - **Archipelago Shop Hints**: what you see at an AP STORE becomes a hint for its owner (on by default). - **Sector Logic** `relaxed` is now called `none` (old YAMLs still work). - A new **`solo_game` preset**: about 7 hours, made for one player alone. - Options are sorted in groups in the Options Creator.
## Traps
- **Hazard Trap**: your next fight's beacon gets a nebula, ion storm, asteroids, a sun or a pulsar. - **Anti-Ship Battery Trap**: your next fight has a battery shooting at you. - **Power Surge Trap**: your next enemy gets a Flagship power surge, again every 25 seconds (lighter in sectors 1 and 2). - **O2 Drain Trap**: every room loses its air at once, never enough to kill a badly hurt crew member. - Hull Breach Trap makes one real breach in a random room. - With Trap Link on, a deal's trap goes to another FTL player only when someone is really on the link. Alone it always hits you.
## Events
- **Engi overclock**: an Engi tech bets he can push your reactor further (Engi and civilian sectors). - **Arms dealer**: rare, in pirate sectors. - The pirates' package gives a vague word on what it is worth. - The Zoltan checkpoint costs 15 scrap for 3 fuel.
## Dashboard and menus
- **In logic marker**: a blue line on the checks you can already do with what you received. - The hangar refuses START on a ship that would not count (out of the seed or not received yet) and says why, and RANDOM SHIP only draws among the ships you have. - The dashboard opens in the hangar too, on the ships page, sorted by checks left with an "Unlocked only" filter. - The start-of-run menu shows each weapon and drone's power and stats, lets you pick which systems come aboard when they don't all fit, offers Oxygen for free to a ship that has none, and a Medbay or Clone Bay swap. - Energy Link shows the shared reserve in fuel and tells you when others put fuel in. - A crew member received with a full crew waits for a free seat. - The connect panel has a real cursor: arrows, Home, End, Delete, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+V at the cursor. - **Universal Tracker** works, without your YAML.
## Fixes
- Locked items and systems really stay out of stores, even with a store opened by an event or Multiverse's store button. - Death Link: holograms, temporary crew and crew taken away by an event are not deaths, and Death Link can be switched off in game. - Fights won offline before a crash are sent on the next connection. - A continued run sends the fights it had counted. - Run start scrap is given once, even when the run started before connecting. - Shop packages count spheres from 1, like Archipelago. - Systemsanity no longer has Install checks for Engines, Oxygen, Piloting and Weapon Control, every ship starts with them. - Random YAMLs always generate. - Ships are named by their class in every menu (Federation Cruiser B).
Thanks to Trapper444 and Yunus for the Spanish and German reviews, and to everyone who tested the betas and reported bugs on the Discord.

entry.title: Sly 2: Band of Thieves v1.2.0
entry.content:
Sly 2 Archipelago implementation. For setup instructions, check out the [README](https://github.com/NikolajDanger/APSly2/blob/main/README.md).
## Changes ### Features - Job skipping! The new `skip_jobs` yaml option allows you to list jobs to skip: they have no checks (or any task checks with `tasksanity`), and the client completes each of them in-game as soon as they become available. You can also skip a job during play with the new `/skip_job <job name>` command, which sends its checks. Running `/skip_job` without a job name lists the jobs you can skip right now. - New pickpocketing modes with the `pickpocket_check_mode` yaml option: `lootsanity` (the old behavior, one check per loot type), `unique` (a check for every new type of loot you pickpocket) and `total` (a check every `pickpocket_check_step` pieces of loot). `pickpocket_check_max` sets how many there are. - Three new traps: - Debt Trap: takes a percentage of your coins, set with the new `debt_trap_percentage` option. - Bottle Sound Trap: plays the clink of a nearby bottle that isn't there. - Hypnosis Trap: hypnotizes the current character. - Trap durations can now be set per trap with the new `trap_duration` option. - The new `ring_link_behavior` option decides whether coins from received items and Debt Traps are shared over ring link. - `scout_thiefnet` now has three options: `show_and_scout` (the old `true`), `show_only` (the old `false`) and the new `hide`, where ThiefNet only shows whose item each one is until it is hinted. - ThiefNet costs can now go up to 99,999 coins, and 5-digit prices display properly in ThiefNet. Please don't actually do this. - The ThiefNet icon theme and text color can now be set in the yaml with the new `thiefnet_icon_theme` and `thiefnet_text_color` options (the `/thiefnet_theme` and `/thiefnet_text` commands still override them in-game). - The `skip_intro` option is back, and skips the Cairo intro straight to the episode select when starting a new game. - The release now includes `sly2_essentials.yaml`, a cut-down template with just the most important options, next to the full template.
### Bug fixes and improvements - Added a "Traps" item group. - Skipping the intro with `/menu` no longer breaks autosaving. - A Sly 1 or Energy Drain Trap received while pickpocketing is no longer lost. - Some client and generation optimizations (faster item/location lookups, loot model install and read cache).

entry.title: Grand Theft Auto III v0.3.0
entry.content:
The game plugin and the APWorld are written again from scratch: this release replaces 0.3.0-alpha.1 entirely. Generate a new room for it.
## What's new
- **Every story mission is a location** (65), plus 8 side missions open from the start on their island: the four RC Toyz missions, the three 4x4 challenges and Multistorey Mayhem. - **Two mission orders** (`mission_order`): - `ordered`: each contact gives a progressive item, and their missions come in story order. - `free`: every mission has its own unlock and can be played in any order. - **Mission markers follow the items**: a locked mission's marker is hidden; once unlocked, its marker shows on the radar and on the ground. Out of the story's order, the mod starts an unlocked mission's marker itself and gives its contact a blip, with one mission per marker at a time. - **Islands open as in the game**: Staunton Island with Last Requests, Shoreside Vale with A Drop in the Ocean. - **Story locks taken off**: two of the game's locks only hold for one order of the missions, and the mod takes both off: - the pause of Pump-Action Pimp, The Fuzz Ball, Dead Skunk in the Trunk and The Getaway between Salvatore's Called a Meeting and Chaperone; - Salvatore's lock between his missions. - **Missions the story closes are checked**: once Last Requests, Waka-Gashira Wipeout! or Grand Theft Aero is passed, the missions it closes for good send their checks with it. - **`need_money` option** (off by default): with it off, Bomb Da Base: Act II and The Exchange start without their $100000 and $500000. - **DeathLink** (`death_link`), with `arrest_is_death` (on by default) to count being busted as a death too. - **Goal**: pass The Exchange. - The game shows each item received. Passed missions are sent again after a reconnection.
## Installation
You need GTA III for PC **version 1.0**, Archipelago **0.6.7** or newer, and the ASI loader [Ultimate ASI Loader](https://github.com/ThirteenAG/Ultimate-ASI-Loader/releases/latest/download/Ultimate-ASI-Loader.zip) (32-bit, `Ultimate-ASI-Loader.zip`, not the `_x64` one).

Put `GTA3Archipelago.asi` in the `scripts` folder next to `gta3.exe` (create it if needed). 3. Double-click `gta3.apworld` to install it in Archipelago, or copy it into Archipelago's `custom_worlds` folder. 4. Write your YAML (`game: Grand Theft Auto III`, with the options above) and generate or join a room. 5. Open **GTA3 Client** from the Archipelago Launcher and connect to the room. 6. Start GTA III and choose **Run Archipelago** in the main menu. Keep GTA3 Client open while you play.
The Steam copy needs a downgrade to 1.0 first: see the README's *Steam version* section.
## Known limitations
- Saving and loading a game is not supported yet: play a run in one session for now. - Only `gta3.exe` 1.0 is supported. (No Steam Version) - With `need_money` on, the logic counts no money: you may have to earn it in the game. - Played far out of the story's order, a mission may still rely on something an earlier one sets up. Please report the ones that break.

entry.content:
# HP2PC_AP v3.0.0
The randomizer now runs on the original PC release of the game with SafeDiscShim, instead of the separate install that v2.12.0 and earlier needed. Everyone needs to set up again: follow the attached `PLAYER_SETUP.md`.
### Upgrading from v2.12.0 or earlier
- **Clean your host.yaml first.** Delete the whole `harry_potter_2_pc_options` block from `host.yaml` in your Archipelago folder before you start the new client. The old block points at the old install, and the client would carry that path over. With the block gone, the client asks for your new install on the first connect and writes fresh settings. - **Replace the apworld.** Swap the old `harry_potter_2_pc.apworld` in `custom_worlds` for this one. - **Start new seeds and saves.** Seeds and saves from the old setup do not carry over. You can leave the old install alone or remove it.
### New
- **Plays on the original game.** Install the game and add SafeDiscShim (free, open source), which lets the game's copy protection run on Windows 10 and 11. No game files ship with this project. - **One install for both game modes.** Vanilla and open castle seeds play on the same install. The client tells the mod which mode the seed uses. - **Borderless window.** The game opens at your monitor's size without a window frame. - **60 fps cap.** The game is held at the speed its physics and timers are tuned for. - **Widescreen view.** The view widens on wide screens, and the menus draw in a centered 4:3 area with black bars at the sides. - **Non-English installs.** The dialogue randomizer works on the game's own language. - **Linux (experimental).** The client finds the game's Wine or Proton prefix and launches the game through Wine. Nobody has confirmed the disc check under Wine yet.
All three display settings are on by default and can be turned off in `host.yaml`.
### Changed
- **Quieter client window.** On connect, the client only says when the mod was updated. Routine details go to the log file. - **Player names with accents** show with the nearest plain letters, since the game cannot draw them. - **Ghost players** wear a pair of grey-blue glasses that stays visible on their see-through face. - **Ghost players use far less network traffic.** Positions only go to players on the same map, once a second, and a player standing still sends none. Everyone else only gets a small "I'm on this map" note every few seconds. Ghosts trail their player by about a second. - **Open castle seeds with nothing to do at the start** are rejected at generation with a hint (add starting spells or turn on secrets), instead of failing to fill.
### Fixed
- **See-through textures** (torch cages, fences, Harry's glasses) no longer draw solid, also after Alt+Tab. - **Trader menus** take clicks again on wide screens. - **Ghost players** carry their wand again. - **A force-closed game** no longer comes back fullscreen at 640x480 on the next launch. - **First start of the game** no longer crashes with `BeginScene failed (DDERR_SURFACELOST)`. The setup guide has you switch the game to windowed before you start it for the first time. - **Freestanding cards** (the Grand Staircase card, the Castle Exterior ledge cards and others) no longer vanish after your first visit to their area. Saves where one already went missing get it back on the next visit. - **Traps and items for other worlds** show their Archipelago logo again instead of being invisible. - **Chests and containers** open again on your next visit when you left their item lying uncollected, so an item that bounced out of reach is never lost. The Entry Hall wooden chest no longer turns into an unopenable box after leaving and returning. - **Cauldron items** drop next to the cauldron instead of landing somewhere out of reach. - **Cards bought from a vendor** stay where they dropped until you pick them up.

entry.title: Slay the Spire II v1.3.0
entry.content:
> [!WARNING] > Both Slay the Spire II and this Archipelago Mod are in active development. As such, while this _is_ playable, expect there to be bugs and limited features. We appreciate your playtesting! > [!IMPORTANT] > **Play on the game's beta branch.** Main-branch support is on thin ice: the mod still runs there, but it's largely untested and new game features won't be supported on it. Multiplayer on the main branch will stop being supported in a future release, because 0.113.0 changed the game's multiplayer code a lot but currently it should still work (probably) ## Setup For installation, YAML configuration, generation and connection instructions, see [the Slay the Spire II setup guide](https://github.com/dlueben1/Slay-the-Spire-2-Archipelago/blob/setup-docs-do-not-delete/world/spire2/docs/setup_en.md). Archipelago **Launcher v0.6.7+** is required for generation. Install **STS2-RitsuLib 0.6.11+** separately. The newest YAML Builder is at [sts2ap.terairk.dev](https://sts2ap.terairk.dev/#/builder), and the mod's **Mod Website & YAML Builder** button opens it. [sts2ap.net](https://sts2ap.net/#/builder) gets the new options later. # Version Information - **Archipelago Client:** 2.1.0 - **APWorld:** 1.3.0 - **Slay the Spire II main branch:** v0.107.1 - **Slay the Spire II beta branch:** v0.113.0 The mod also includes a build for v0.111.0, so it keeps working if the main branch moves there before the next release. # Changelist ## Major changes ### Beta 0.113.0 and the Fool The mod now supports beta **0.113.0**, including its new character, **the Fool**. Add `Fool` to `characters` Dread and Blitz merchants come back as AP options below. ### Dread Mode `dread_mode: true` makes every run a Dread run, the game's Dread mode: each act has a Dominion (an extra combat rule set by that act's boss), bosses are stronger, and you gain an Ascender's Bane at the start of Acts 2 and 3. Your Ascension and Ascension Down settings apply as usual; the base game plays Dread at Ascension 10. Run Modifiers and enemy scaling still stack on top. Logic doesn't account for it and no plans to do so to make generation lenient. In multiplayer the host's setting applies to the whole run. ### Blitz Merchants `blitz_merchant_chance` (0-100) gives each shop a chance to be the game's **Blitz merchant** instead: six offers and three free picks in place of a shop's stock. Shop Sanity checks are still sold there, on the same AP page as a normal shop. Which shops are Blitz merchants depends only on the seed and the shop's place on the map, so reloading doesn't reroll them. Three free picks are worth a lot more than a normal shop visit, and logic ignores it entirely; at high values gold has little use. Pair it with harder Challenges. **Should work in multiplayer (the host's chance applies to the whole run) but may have bugs.** Dread Mode and Blitz Merchants need the beta branch. A slot with either still connects on the main branch: you get a notice such as "This game version does not have: Dread Mode (runs are standard runs)", and the slot plays standard runs with normal shops. ### Challenges A new set of **opt-in** options for people who find the game too easy, or who keep going out of logic because they're good at the game. Logic stays at roughly vanilla-run power, so instead of rescaling logic the idea is to make runs harder in ways that mostly leave Act 1 alone and ramp up in Acts 2 and 3. **None of these change logic, and they're all off by default.** - **Run Modifiers:** pick any of RisingStrength, EscalatingBuffs, ShrinkingRests, MountingCurses, MountingBanes, CursedRun, ExtraAscendersBane, SlowStart, FrailStart and DangerousUnknowns. They stack on top of Ascension. - **Enemy HP Scaling / Enemy Damage Scaling:** up to +15% enemy max HP or damage in Acts 2 and 3. - **Strict Card Rewards:** you can no longer look through every card reward in the AP menu before picking. Opening one locks the others until you take a card or Discard it, like a normal card reward after a fight. You have to make local choices instead of picking the best card out of 15. - **Hidden Intents, Hidden Health, Hidden Piles, Hidden Map and Hidden Cards:** each hides part of the UI until you receive its **Sight** item (Intent Sight, Health Sight, Pile Sight, Map Sight, Card Sight). One copy is enough to undo it for every character; the option value is how many copies go in the pool, so a second copy just makes it easier to find. Hidden Map only shows the rooms you can move to next and puts a closed eye on everything further ahead. **Hidden Cards:** every card looks like an unseen card in the Compendium: blurred art, an unknown name and text, "?" for the energy cost, and no tooltips. Useless for veterans but maybe cool for new people In multiplayer, the host's Run Modifiers and enemy scaling apply to the whole run. The YAML Builder has a new **Challenges** step for all of these. You have to opt in to see them. ### Custom Shop A new opt-in option for more varied shops. Normally a shop sells 2 Attacks, 2 Skills, a Power and 2 colorless cards; with `random_shop_cards: true` (**Custom Shop Cards**) each of the 7 card slots rolls its own kind instead, so a shop can be all Powers, all Rares, or all colorless cards. Eight weights (`shop_attack_weight`, `shop_skill_weight`, `shop_power_weight`, `shop_common_weight`, `shop_uncommon_weight`, `shop_rare_weight`, `shop_colorless_weight`, `shop_event_weight`; none, low, medium or high) decide how often each kind turns up. The new Event weight lets a slot sell Event cards, such as Trash Heap's. **Custom Shop Relics** (`random_shop_relics`) and **Custom Shop Potions** (`random_shop_potions`) do the same for the 3 relic and 3 potion slots, with their own weights: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Shop, Event and **Ancient** relics, and Common, Uncommon, Rare, other characters' and Event potions. Ancient relics cost 400 gold, Event relics 250, Event potions 100 and Event cards about 100. It works with or without Shop Sanity, adds no locations and doesn't change logic. If there's no card left of the kind a slot rolled, it falls back to the nearest rarity or type. ### YAML Builder: import and autosave - **Import YAML:** load an existing YAML (from the builder or written by hand) back into the builder and keep editing it. Anything the builder can't show, like random or weighted values, is listed as a warning. - **Autosave:** your answers and the step you're on are kept in your browser, so closing the tab doesn't lose them. **Start over** clears them. - **Filler slots:** Bonus Items and Challenges show how many filler slots you have left, and the builder won't let you pick more than generation can fit. - **Other QOL**: such as one button press to enable all ascensions or being able to duplicate bonus items without going through the menu again and again. ### Gold, Potion, Shop and Campfire Sanity are on by default These four now default to **on** because more random = more fun and they only improve the experience imo. The YAML Builder starts with them ticked. It's one of those settings that people usually recommend to have on anyway. Campfire sanity is more debatable but it makes logic way more varied. ### Logic overhaul (v3) The new logic from 2.0 made item order a lot more varied, but playtesting a 33-character seed showed some places where logic asked for things that didn't line up with how a run actually goes, so you'd end up going out of logic just to reach your Sphere 1 checks. This update is about making logic feel more natural rather than harder or easier. - **Shop slots** come into logic based on the gold you'd realistically have, including combat gold, instead of a flat 50 AP gold. With cheap shop pricing, Act 1 shops are in logic from the start; with full prices, they need more gold. - **Campfires:** the first campfire checks of each act are no longer "early" checks, because a campfire can't appear until several floors in. - **Act 1** expects 7 fights instead of 8. - **Elites** have their own track in each act, separate from bomb-rushing ? rooms. Your first elite relic can be in logic before the rest of late Act 1. - **Relics Available Anytime** is now properly modelled. - **Modded characters** get the same default starter power as vanilla characters instead of hard gates on their progressive starters. Almost every well-made character mod defines Orobas mappings. - Fewer hard gates, e.g. you no longer need a Smith to beat the Act 1 boss. Gold matters more. `use_new_logic: false` still gives you the old (1.1.x) logic. ### AP Run Graph and Past AP Runs There's an end-of-run graph showing your HP across the run alongside when your AP checks happened, and you can look back at old AP runs from the new **Past AP Runs** button on the main menu. Runs that never reached a game-over screen are grouped by seed and still count towards that seed's progress. Runs you saved and quit before dying now open a full recap too. An unfinished run gets its own card while it's still that character's newest run on the seed (shown as **In progress**), or once a later run replaced it after floor 5; earlier replaced runs fold in as restarts. The singleplayer checkpoint picker and multiplayer campaign picker also got a redesign to match. Checkpoints are laid out per act and show the room, floor, HP, gold, deck size and relics from the save itself. To make room, the **Install APWorld button is gone** from the main menu. It only worked on Windows with a default Archipelago install, didn't help the person actually hosting, and installing APWorlds from GitHub is where the source can be checked anyway. ### Game updates Prepares the mod for game updates so it breaks loudly instead of quietly: - If the mod fails to start, you now get the game's red **"Loaded N mods WITH ERRORS!"** label instead of a client that looks loaded but is only half working. - If the game updates before we do, the mod will try running the build for the previous game version, after checking that everything it uses still exists. If something's missing it fails at startup. The version overlay says "(vX build, untested on this game version)" when this happens. - Connecting to a slot whose vanilla character doesn't exist on your game version (e.g. the Fool on main) now warns you instead of refusing to connect. - The mod ships an extra build for 0.111.0, so the main branch moving there doesn't need a new release. ---
Full details ### Beta 0.113.0 - The Fool uses the default starter power in logic until its starter values (Foolish Shot to Divine Shot, Song Bow to Storyteller) are reviewed. Its cards, relics and potions are unlocked like every other character's, and its card pool joins cross-character rewards. - **Lord's Parasol** can't appear in multiplayer runs with Shop Sanity on 0.113.0. The game now replays it on every player's machine, and the other machines would buy the locked AP shop slots too, which could leave the lobby waiting on a choice that never comes. Older game versions are unchanged. - Shops were ported to 0.113.0's new shop code, including Custom Shop and the AP shop page. - The missing-character warning also covers a base-game character from the other game branch. ### Challenges - Run Modifiers in detail: - **RisingStrength:** elites and bosses start each combat with 1 Strength in Act 2 and 2 in Act 3. - **EscalatingBuffs:** enemies start combat with one random buff in Act 2 and two in Act 3 (Strength, Plating, Thorns, Artifact, Regen, Curl Up, Vigor or Slippery). - **ShrinkingRests:** resting heals 25% in Act 2 and 20% in Act 3 instead of 30%. - **MountingCurses:** a random curse at the start of Acts 2 and 3. **CursedRun** is the base game's version, which also curses Act 1. They stack. - **MountingBanes:** an extra Ascender's Bane at the start of Acts 2 and 3. **ExtraAscendersBane** gives one at the start of the run. They stack. - **SlowStart:** draw 1 fewer card on the first turn of each combat. - **FrailStart:** start with 10% less max HP. - **DangerousUnknowns:** ? rooms lean towards fights and elites. This does reach combat and relic checks sooner than logic expects, but events are everyone's safe haven, so it's in for fun. Juzu Bracelet never appears with it. - Strict Card Rewards: Skip, the map, the deck and closing the menu keep the revealed reward for later. With Pael's Wing, Sacrifice replaces Discard. In singleplayer, an unopened card reward depends on what you took before it, so loading a checkpoint and picking differently changes it. The mod's settings can override this option. - Hidden Health keeps Block visible but hides health bars, the top bar HP, and poison/doom previews. - Hidden Piles shows "?" for the draw, discard and exhaust piles, and they can't be opened. The deck button still works. - Hidden Map keeps boss and Ancient icons visible. - Hidden Map: hovering or clicking a map legend entry no longer enlarges hidden rooms of that type, including with MintySpire2's sticky legend highlights. - Hidden Intents also hides the Intent Graph mod's overlay. - Hidden Cards reuses the game's own unseen-card look from the Compendium. The card type (Attack/Skill/Power) and the frame and banner colours still show. - The Hidden options turn themselves off when Include Floor Checks is off, like Progressive Starters and Ascension Downs, instead of failing generation (Sight items take floor-check filler slots). - Dread Mode: the game normally only offers Dread at Ascension 10 once every character has cleared it; in AP any Ascension set works, because Dread's rules add to the Ascension values rather than replacing them. AP runs don't change the game's Dread win streaks, in singleplayer or multiplayer. ### Logic and generation - Later ordinary card rewards count for a bit more power than before. - Card strength uses per-count tables from a card draft model. - Shops ask for enough gold to buy their most expensive listed checks. - Only relics a run can actually claim are counted. - Each elite fight and chest relic has its own region. - The climb to Act 3 is split between the Act 2 boss and Early Act 3. - Sparse worlds (no floor, gold or potion checks) only fall back to old logic when they're the only world in the generation; next to other players they use new logic. - Trap Chance with every trap weight set to none is now an option error instead of a failed generation. ### Cards, relics and rewards - **Lasting Candy is back.** Its counter now moves on every AP card reward, so every second one you open gets the extra Power. It was disabled because the counter only moved on combats. - Removed the multiplayer card reveal check. It added a network message for every reveal, and its 15 second timeout could disable AP claims for the whole run even when nothing was wrong. The game's own checksum already catches real mismatches. - Custom Shop: Mad Science and the event pool's Ancient cards are never sold. Event potions cost 100 so Foul Potion can't be bought and thrown at the merchant for profit. A Courier restock stays vanilla, so purchases can't chain into more random stock. ### Website and YAML - New **Challenges** step in the YAML Builder, before Progression. - **Remove Overpowered Relics** is now on the website. - YAMLs generated by the website now include the template's comments, so you can hand-edit them later instead of redoing everything on the website. Comments in the preview are greyed out. - New options are at the bottom of the YAML. - **Import YAML** and **autosave** (see above). - New **Custom Shop** section in Checks & Rewards for cards, relics and potions, and a **Hidden Cards** question in Challenges. - The Fool in the character step, with a "Beta branch only" badge and a warning on the Review page. The portrait grid splits into two rows once there are more than six characters. - **Dread Mode** and **Blitz Merchant Chance** in Challenges, labelled beta-only. - Card Sight counts towards the builder's filler budget. - Ascensions: a checkbox at the top of each column selects or clears the whole column. Selecting every Down skips Swarming Elites, and a red warning shows when Swarming Elites is off or its Down is ticked. - Bonus Items: a Duplicate button on each row. - The Progressive Items explainer is rewritten for the current items. - The website footer now credits Mega Crit and says the mod isn't affiliated with them. Copyright reasons - The mod's **Mod Website & YAML Builder** button and the option links point at sts2ap.terairk.dev until sts2ap.net catches up. ### Fixes and other changes - Shop Sanity prices no longer use your shop's RNG. In multiplayer, pricing the AP page threw the other players' copy of your shop out of step, so your later shops and Blitz offers could roll differently on each machine. An AP check's price is now also the same on every visit. - When a run doesn't get its Run Modifiers, the log now says why. - Removed some error spam from the logs at run start and with Archaic Tooth. - Splash and Kaleidoscope fail loudly if a game update moves the code they change, instead of quietly keeping AP's character locks on their choices. - Internal: game API differences are now named after game versions, and every patch target is checked by the compiler. There's also a script that reports what a game update means for the mod, so updating the mod after a patch should be a lot quicker.
## Already in 2.0.1 and 2.0.2 If you're coming from 2.0.0, these shipped in the 2.0.x hotfixes: - **Missing character mods:** you can connect without every modded character installed. Defect is always available and counts checks for the missing characters. - **Steam overlay and link joins** work for multiplayer, not just the in-game Join button. - **Remove Overpowered Relics** option (Pael's Growth and Glitter from Anytime Ancients, Prayer Wheel and White Star everywhere). - A copy button for modded character IDs, more predefined modded characters, and a much smaller data package. - Singleplayer runs keep going when the AP connection drops, reconnecting in the background for up to five minutes. - Fixed AP reward menus failing in multiplayer between Windows and Linux/macOS players (2.0.2). - Boss Gold in the in-game tracker, the second boss removed from the map when Double Boss is removed mid-act, and a shorter Sea Glass title for modded characters. ## Version compatibility Use the updated APWorld and client together. The Challenges options, Sight items, Custom Shop, Dread Mode, Blitz Merchants and the Fool need both. The Fool, Dread Mode and Blitz Merchants also need the game's beta branch. Everyone in a multiplayer lobby should use the same client version and game branch. The **Neutral Shop Card Slot** item is now called **Shop Colorless Card Slot** (same item ID). Update any `start_inventory`, plando or hint commands that name it. ## Known Issues/Limitations - **Main branch:** largely untested and gets no new features. Main-branch multiplayer will stop being supported in a future release. - Dread Mode: a Double Boss Ascension Down that arrives during Act 3 removes the second boss but keeps its Dominion until the boss fight; after a reload the first boss's Dominion applies. - In multiplayer, AP menu rewards can only be claimed outside combat; Death Fragments are disabled. **Anytime** Ancient rewards are recommended. - Hidden Cards still shows each card's type and frame colour, and you can work a card out from the energy it spends or what it does when played. Basically tried to do the minimum amount of code here to minimise patch conflicts with other mods

entry.title: Team Fortress 2 Mann vs Machine v1.18.8r2
entry.content: ## Changes ### Fixed - **The debug bundle no longer tells Windows players to press Repair when Repair cannot help.** SigMod already checks the game files it reads, and when it finds them right the summary now says so, says the crash comes from SigMod on Windows, and explains how to play without it until a fix ships. - **The debug bundle sees a Linux server that crashes on `replay_srv.so`.** It used to report "nothing matched" while the server restarted every few seconds. It now names the error and gives the command that finds the missing 32-bit system library. ## Windows Download **`tf2ap.exe`** above. Run it. It installs everything else. Windows will warn you, and it is a false positive. The exe unpacks archives and starts a game server without a code signature, which looks like a virus to a scanner. Click **More info**, then **Run anyway**, or check it below first. [Full guide](https://m-this.github.io/tf2-archipelago/en/setup/install-windows.html) ## Linux Download **`tf2ap-linux-amd64`**. Run it. It installs everything else. ```sh chmod +x tf2ap-linux-amd64 ./tf2ap-linux-amd64 ``` [Full guide](https://m-this.github.io/tf2-archipelago/en/setup/install-linux.html) ## Docker Download **`compose.yaml`** and **`env.example`**: ```sh mkdir mann-vs-archipelago && cd mann-vs-archipelago base=https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/releases/latest/download curl -fsSLO "$base/compose.yaml" curl -fsSL -o .env "$base/env.example" ``` Set `SRCDS_RCONPW` in `.env`, then: ```sh docker compose --profile seed run --rm seed # writes ./seed docker compose up -d ``` Upload the file from `seed/` at [archipelago.gg/uploads](https://archipelago.gg/uploads) and put the room's port into `AP_PORT`. [Full guide](https://m-this.github.io/tf2-archipelago/en/setup/install.html) ## Other assets | File | For | | --- | --- | | `tf2_mvm.apworld` | The official Archipelago app. | | `tf2_archipelago.smx` | A SourceMod server the launcher and compose file don't manage. | | `tf2-defender-bots.zip` | The bots for that same server. Unzip into `tf/`. | | `meta.json`, `items.json`, `missions.json` | The item and check tables, for reference. | ## Checking what you downloaded **`SHA256SUMS`** is attached to this release. It holds the hash of every file here, computed by the workflow that built them. ```powershell Get-FileHash tf2ap.exe -Algorithm SHA256 # Windows ``` ```sh sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing # Linux ``` Each binary carries a signed record of the commit and the workflow that built it: ```sh gh attestation verify tf2ap.exe --repo m-this/tf2-archipelago ``` The binaries are scanned on VirusTotal, and the reports are linked at the end of these notes. Expect a few heuristic detections and no named malware family. The source is all in the repository, and `make launcher` rebuilds the exe on your own machine. ## Code signing policy Free code signing for open source projects, provided by [SignPath.org](https://signpath.org), with a certificate from the [SignPath Foundation](https://signpath.org). > [!WARNING] > The application is open, not granted. Nothing is signed yet: `tf2ap.exe` ships > unsigned, and Windows warns about it until that changes. ## What's Changed * feat(stability): known-failure list for the daily report by @m-this in https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/pull/259 **Full Changelog**: https://github.com/m-this/tf2-archipelago/compare/v1.18.7...v1.18.8 ## VirusTotal - [`tf2ap.exe`](https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file-analysis/ZDc0MmUwOTljODE3Mzk3NDlmMDMwZTUwMTY1NDZhZjI6MTc5NDU5Mjg0OA==/detection) - [`tf2ap-linux-amd64`](https://www.virustotal.com/gui/file-analysis/NTZiMGIxMTBhYThlMTczYWY4NTFmYjExOTJlZjQwMzg6MTc5NDU5Mjg1MQ==/detection)

entry.title: One Piece Unlimited Cruise 1 v1.0.0
entry.content:
This week's update is... **SUPER!** :star: There are a handful of major features within this update, as well as some extra options and QoL changes! This is our first build I'm happy to call feature complete!
> Generate a new seed with this version and the new `OPUC1.yaml`. Older YAMLs fall back to the defaults for the new options.
## What's New? ### **The Cave Isle, The Underwater Passage** The main feature of this update, adds the 4th Island to the run, meaning all Islands are in the Archipelago! This means Locations for all the bosses, ambushes, shrines, stone monuments, treasure chests, as well as new locations for Usopp's Workshop / Sanji's Kitchen / Chopper's Pharmacy / Fishsanity / Creaturesanity with all the Cave Isle has to offer. Moles are finally in logic with the addition of the Cave Isle, so all the Obstructed Path Build Sites on the other Islands can now be accessed, adding Nightmare Luffy, Rampaging Chopper and all sorts of other Chests and Monuments into Logic.
### **Franky's Supplies & Extra Recipes** Our 2nd biggest addition this update! After digging into the menu data, I managed to find quite a bit of early development data for UC2, including the 2nd Development Menu, left completely unused in UC1. I've added this menu into the game as a 4th crafting menu that you access via the Side Doors on the Sunny, replacing the Storage's Touchspots. Here, you can trade in Old Gold Coins for various items that can be pretty tedious to get normally, such as Dial Fragments. This menu also has 20+ Archipelago Item crafting recipes. A New Feature has been added called "Extra Recipes", which fills in the rest of the 32-slot crafting menus for Development/Cooking/Pharmacy, adding **30+** new Crafting Recipes for Archipelago Items! The Materials needed for both these new Extra Recipes as well as all the Archipelago Items in Franky's Supplies are randomized at seed generation! *(You can still access the Storage via the Menu)*
This is a completely separate crafting menu from Usopp's Workshop, so instead of Art of Development, the required skill to level up to unlock more recipes is Franky's Supply Skill, which has been renamed to "Art of Supplying". It still reduces Build Site costs as usual. Old Gold Coins have become a lot easier to find when Franky's Supplies is enabled. The following changes get applied: - The Flour/Hardtack Ration Barrels have a 50% chance to drop Old Gold Coins instead. - Golden Hercules now drop 1-5 Old Gold Coins instead of Sticky Sap. *(You can still obtain Sticky Sap from regular Hercules Beetles. Sticky Sap is also one of the trade items you can receive from Franky's Supplies)* - All the "Junk" Salvage Items you pick up from Fishing become Old Gold Coins. - The Sea Anemones on the Cave Isle drop Old Gold Coins instead of Black Orbs. - Thousand Sunny's dust spots drop Old Gold Coins instead. - Old Gold Coins have also been added to the "Other Items" filler pool. *(Including Packages)*
### **Energy Link Support** Energy Link has been added! A tab has been added to the client, where you can manage Gabri's 6 energy bars. Gabri takes 100 Energy to fill a bar. For Energy Link, 1 Energy = 10 MJ, so 1 bar of Gabri Energy is 1 GJ. There is a 20% cut when converting. Gold Energy takes twice as much to fill, but also gives out twice the amount of energy when converting. This makes grinding energy a lot smoother, as you can move energy between the bars, so I highly recommend using this option even if this is the only game using Energy Link.
### **Other New Features/Options** - **Archipelago Client Icon** - The ONE PIECE: Unlimited Cruise 1 AP Client now has a unique icon in the Archipelago Launcher. - **In-Game Archipelago Messages** - Items you receive or send to other players will be displayed as text in-game. *(You can tweak it/turn it off via the OPUC1 Client)* - **Extra Final Door Requirement** - You can choose if you want to defeat all Island Bosses/All Bosses, before goaling. - **Gabri Energy Items** - You can now choose to have all Gabri Level Ups to be per colour. - **How Many Gabri Level Items** - You can choose how many of those per colour upgrades exist. - **Starting Gabri Energy** - You can choose your starting Gabri Energy. *(always starting with at least 1 Blue Energy to avoid getting hard gated in the Prologue)* - **The Wherever Cannon** - You can choose if the Wherever Cannon is unlocked via completing its Build Site, or have it be directly unlocked on the Sunny upon finding the AP item. - **Materialsanity** - Adds 40 "Got" Locations for first-time pick up of a Material. - **Expanded Storage** - The Storage can now hold up to 45 Items. - **Easier Fish** - Fish have a 50% weaker pull strength when reeling in. - **Better Plant Drop Rates** - Now includes Ashes and Mysterious Seaweed *(both now 80% drop rate from their natural sources)*
### Known Issue Don't load a save after quitting to the title screen - it can hang on a black screen. Close the game, start it again (client at the title screen) and load from there. Your save is fine.
